questions.q: The definition of a podocytopathy on this page places the primary injury on the podocyte.
opts: False — podocytopathies are defined by primary mesangial cell injury
False — the term is reserved for diseases of the glomerular basement membrane
True — and every disease in the group carries the same risk of chronic kidney disease
True — the podocyte is named as the primary target, not the mesangium or the endothelium
questions.exp: Glomerular diseases that primarily affect podocytes. (Book p762)

questions.q: The clinical presentation list of glomerular diseases repeated here runs from asymptomatic and macroscopic hematuria through nephrotic/nephritic syndromes to RPGN and:
questions.exp: Presentation list ends with chronic glomerulonephritis. (Book p762)

questions.q: Match each podocytopathy with its CKD-risk label — 1) Minimal change disease 2) FSGS 3) Membranous nephropathy … A) >2/3rd → CKD even with Rx B) No risk for CKD C) 1/3rd → CKD if not treated
questions.exp: Without podocytopenia: MCD (no CKD risk); with podocytopenia: FSGS >2/3rd → CKD even with Rx; MN 1/3rd → CKD if not treated. (Book p762)

questions.q: The with-podocytopenia branch (the CKD-risk branch) names FSGS, membranous nephropathy and diabetic nephropathy; the entity NOT placed on that branch is:
questions.exp: With podocytopenia: FSGS, MN, diabetic nephropathy (DN). (Book p762)

questions.q: Match each 2° MCD item with its book annotation — 1) NSAIDs 2) Gold 3) Highlighted malignancy … A) Hodgkin's disease B) MN > MCD C) MCD > MN
questions.exp: NSAIDs (MCD > MN); gold (MN > MCD); malignancy highlight: Hodgkin's disease. (Book p762)

questions.q: The allergy branch of 2° MCD causes lists atopic rhinitis, atopic dermatitis, asthma and:
questions.exp: Allergy: atopic rhinitis, atopic dermatitis, asthma, post-immunization. (Book p762)

questions.q: Sezary syndrome, bracketed inside the malignancy line for minimal change disease, is described as a cutaneous T cell lymphoma.
opts: True — the bracket reads cutaneous T cell lymphoma
False — Sezary syndrome is the B-cell leukemia of that line
False — the bracket identifies it as a plasma cell dyscrasia
True — and Hodgkin's disease carries the same bracket
questions.exp: Malignancy: Hodgkin's disease; Sezary syndrome (cutaneous T cell lymphoma); CLL. (Book p762)

questions.q: The 100/0 rule of MCD presentation states that every patient of MCD presents with:
questions.exp: 100/0 rule: every patient of MCD → nephrotic syndrome. (Book p762)

questions.q: Hypertension, AKI and microhematuria are written as absent in MCD; the feature that IS expected is:
questions.exp: Hypertension, AKI & microhematuria absent; nephrotic syndrome present (100/0 rule). (Book p762)

questions.q: Which MCD presentation statement is TRUE?
opts: AKI is a routine presenting feature of MCD
Every MCD patient presents with nephrotic syndrome, with hypertension, AKI and microhematuria absent
A quarter of MCD patients present with isolated hematuria
MCD commonly presents with hypertensive crisis
questions.exp: 100/0 rule; hypertension, AKI & microhematuria absent. (Book p762)

questions.q: Fill up: The MCD rule that every patient presents with nephrotic syndrome is the ______ rule.
questions.exp: 100/0 rule: every patient of MCD → nephrotic syndrome. (Book p762)

questions.q: Every one of these drugs appears in the drug line for secondary FSGS EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Dasatinib (tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI)) among 2° FSGS drugs. (Book p763)

questions.q: All of the following sit in the 2° FSGS drug list EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Gold belongs to the MN/MCD drug lists; FSGS drugs are pamidronate, anabolic steroids, heroin, sirolimus, dasatinib, IFN α. (Book p763)

questions.q: A 28-year-old with HIV develops nephrotic-range proteinuria and a rising creatinine; the infection line of the secondary FSGS list is read. Which diseases sit on that line?
opts: HIV-associated nephropathy, parvovirus B19, EBV and CMV
questions.exp: Infections: HIVAN, parvo B19, EBV, CMV. (Book p763)

questions.q: The miscellaneous causes of secondary FSGS include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Miscellaneous: sickle cell anemia, obesity, congenital cyanotic heart disease. (Book p763)

questions.q: Fill up: In primary FSGS, soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor and cardiotrophin-like cytokine 1 are bracketed together as a circulating ______ factor.
questions.exp: suPAR + CLC-1 bracketed as circulating permeability factor. (Book p763)

questions.q: Match each genetic form with its gene product — 1) NPHS1 gene 2) NPHS2 gene 3) α actin 4, TRPC 6 … A) Podocin B) Nephrin C) Autosomal dominant adolescent form
questions.exp: NPHS1 → nephrin; NPHS2 → podocin; α actin 4, TRPC 6 = autosomal dominant. (Book p763)

questions.q: Match each congenital-NS column with its feature — 1) NPHS1 histology 2) NPHS2 histology 3) α actin 4 / TRPC 6 inheritance … A) Autosomal dominant B) Diffuse mesangial sclerosis C) FSGS
questions.exp: NPHS1: present at birth, diffuse mesangial sclerosis; NPHS2: by 3-5 years, FSGS; α actin 4/TRPC 6: autosomal dominant, adolescents. (Book p763)

questions.q: The genetic forms of congenital nephrotic syndrome are resistant to immunosuppression therapy; the only Rx written is:
questions.exp: Resistant to immunosuppression therapy; only Rx: transplantation. (Book p763)

questions.q: Secondary perihilar FSGS after removal of a pathological kidney is attributed on this page to hyperfiltration injury with glomerular hypertrophy.
opts: False — the page blames recurrence of the circulating permeability factor
False — it is classified among the antigen-associated primary forms
True — and this form is managed with immunosuppression rather than ACE blockade
True — the printed chain is removal of the kidney, hyperfiltration with glomerular hypertrophy, then perihilar FSGS
questions.exp: Removal of pathological kidney → remaining nephrons undergo hyperfiltration injury (glomerular hypertrophy) → 2° perihilar FSGS. (Book p763)

questions.q: 2° perihilar FSGS runs a slow course with good prognosis and asymptomatic proteinuria; its causes are VUR, U/l RAS and stone/mass, and progression can be slowed using:
questions.exp: Causes: VUR, U/l RAS, stone/mass; progression can be slowed using ACE (−). (Book p763)

questions.q: The FSGS 75/25 rule states that 75% present with nephrotic syndrome while 25% show:
questions.exp: 75%: nephrotic syndrome; 25%: asymptomatic/nephrotic proteinuria without syndrome. (Book p764)

questions.q: The 25% asymptomatic arm of the 75/25 rule points to 2° perihilar FSGS (other cause: DM); the instruction written for this arm is:
questions.exp: 2° perihilar FSGS (other cause: DM) → do not give immunosuppression. (Book p764)

questions.q: The drug causes of 2° MN are gold, NSAIDs, d-penicillamine, captopril and:
questions.exp: MN drugs: gold, NSAIDs, d-penicillamine, captopril, mercury. (Book p764)

questions.q: The infection causes of 2° MN are hepatitis B virus, syphilis and:
questions.exp: Infections: HBV, syphilis, schistosomiasis. (Book p764)

questions.q: For rheumatoid arthritis, the ranking of glomerular lesions printed on this page puts secondary amyloidosis ahead of membranous nephropathy.
opts: False — membranous nephropathy is ranked ahead of secondary amyloidosis
False — only membranous nephropathy is listed for rheumatoid arthritis
True — and sarcoidosis is ranked in the same order
True — the line reads secondary amyloidosis ahead of membranous nephropathy
questions.exp: Rheumatoid arthritis: m/c glomerular manifestations: 2° amyloidosis > MN. (Book p764)

questions.q: Sarcoidosis and IgG4-related disease, among MN autoimmune associations, produce:
questions.exp: Sarcoidosis, IgG4 related disease: tubulointerstitial disease > glomerular (MN). (Book p764)

questions.q: The malignancy linked to 2° MN is solid organ adenocarcinoma, and the most important one listed is:
questions.exp: Solid organ adenocarcinoma: colorectal carcinoma (most important). (Book p764)

questions.q: 1° MN is antibody-associated; the antibody written is:
questions.exp: 1° MN: anti PLA2R (anti phospholipase A2 receptor antibody). (Book p764)

questions.q: The MN presentation 70/30 rule splits into 70% nephrotic syndrome and 30% asymptomatic (microhematuria & proteinuria); the thrombosis note says MN carries:
questions.exp: 70/30 rule; maximum risk of thrombosis. (Book p764)

questions.q: The note on this page lists membranous nephropathy among the diseases associated with d-penicillamine, beside Wilson's disease, aplastic anemia and myasthenia gravis.
opts: False — the fourth disease is minimal change disease
False — the note ties d-penicillamine to FSGS
True — and gold is named in the same note as the drug for Wilson's disease
True — membranous nephropathy is the fourth disease of that note
questions.exp: d-penicillamine: Wilson's disease, aplastic anemia, myasthenia gravis, MN. (Book p764)

questions.q: The m/c cause of adult-onset nephrotic syndrome and of NS in children are respectively:
questions.exp: m/c cause of adult onset nephrotic syndrome: MN; m/c cause of NS in children: MCD. (Book p764)

questions.q: Alongside the 90% of childhood nephrotic syndrome, what share of ADULT nephrotic syndrome is attributed to minimal change disease on this page?
questions.exp: AKA lipoid nephrosis; 90% of childhood NS; 10-15% of adult NS. (Book p765)

questions.q: The peak age group for MCD and its sex preponderance are:
questions.exp: Boys > girls; peak age group: 2-7 yrs. (Book p765)

questions.q: Selective proteinuria, losing only albumin & transferrin, is seen in few cases of MCD; the bullet for MCD proteinuria in general reads:
questions.exp: MCD bullet: non-selective proteinuria; selective (albumin & transferrin only) in few cases. (Book p765)

questions.q: The podocyte changes in MCD are effacement of foot process with ↑ CD80 expression and ↑ angiopoietin-like 4 peptide, causing:
opts: Loss of negative charges → leaking of proteins
questions.exp: ↑ CD80 and ↑ angiopoietin like 4 peptide → loss of negative charges → leaking of proteins. (Book p765)

questions.q: Fill up: In MCD the podocyte surface molecule whose expression rises, alongside angiopoietin-like 4 peptide, is ______.
questions.exp: ↑ CD80 expression. (Book p765)

questions.q: Two-thirds of MCD relapses follow URTI/LRTI; the relapse-prevention Rx written at onset of URTI/LRTI is:
questions.exp: Relapse 2/3rd d/t URTI/LRTI; Rx: prednisolone (0.5 mg/kg) at onset of URTI/LRTI. (Book p765)

questions.q: After 4 weeks of steroids, the steroid-resistance share that triggers a biopsy to r/o FSGS is:
questions.exp: 5-10% resistance → biopsy taken to r/o FSGS (can cause CKD). (Book p765)

questions.q: Among steroid responders, the flowchart splits into 25% cured with no relapse, 25% infrequent relapse (steroid & taper off) and:
opts: 50% FRNS (≥2 relapse in 6 months, ≥4 in 1 year)
questions.exp: Respond to steroids: 25% cured, 25% infrequent relapse, 50% FRNS (≥2 in 6 months, ≥4 in 1 year). (Book p765)

questions.q: FRNS is started on steroid-sparing agents; the preferred one written is:
questions.exp: FRNS: steroid sparing agents: oral cyclophosphamide (preferred). (Book p765)

questions.q: SDNS (≥2 relapses within 14 days of stopping steroid or while tapering) is treated with the agent labelled best, which is:
questions.exp: SDNS treated using: MMF (best); rituximab. (Book p765)

questions.q: In the resistant arm, a normal biopsy may still miss FSGS; genetic studies then decide, with a normal result starting CNI and a positive FSGS result leading to:
questions.exp: Normal (sometimes FSGS can be missed) → genetic studies; normal → CNI; FSGS → transplant. (Book p765)

questions.sec: Biopsy & IF: MCD, IgM Nephropathy, FSGS
questions.q: In MCD, biopsy (light microscopy, PAS) and immunofluorescence are both:
questions.exp: Biopsy: normal; IF: normal (light microscopy: normal glomerulus, PAS stain). (Book p766)

questions.sec: Biopsy & IF: MCD, IgM Nephropathy, FSGS
questions.q: IgM nephropathy, a variant of MCD, shows mesangial matrix expansion on biopsy, IgM +ve on IF and:
questions.exp: IgM nephropathy: variant of MCD; mesangial matrix expansion; IF IgM +ve; poor prognosis compared to MCD. (Book p766)

questions.sec: Biopsy & IF: MCD, IgM Nephropathy, FSGS
questions.q: With Apo L1 polymorphisms in FSGS, what proportion of patients develop CKD by 10 years?
questions.exp: Associated with Apo L1 polymorphisms; 70% develop CKD by 10 years. (Book p766)

questions.sec: Biopsy & IF: MCD, IgM Nephropathy, FSGS
questions.q: Fill up: In the biopsy definitions of FSGS, 'focal' means fewer than ______ percent of glomeruli are involved.
questions.exp: Focal: <50% glomeruli involved; segmental: only a portion of glomeruli involved. (Book p766)

questions.sec: Biopsy & IF: MCD, IgM Nephropathy, FSGS
questions.q: The sclerosis chain written for FSGS runs: podocyte lost in urine → podocytopenia → GBM synechiae with parietal epithelial cell →
questions.exp: Eosinophilic hyaline material obliterating glomeruli: podocyte lost in urine → podocytopenia → GBM synechiae with parietal epithelial cell → sclerosis. (Book p766)

questions.sec: Biopsy & IF: MCD, IgM Nephropathy, FSGS
questions.q: IF in FSGS shows focal IgM ± C3; in 2° FSGS the IF is:
questions.exp: IF: focal IgM ± C3; 2° FSGS: IF negative. (Book p766)

questions.sec: Biopsy & IF: MCD, IgM Nephropathy, FSGS
questions.q: The FSGS treatment ladder uses steroid 1 mg/kg/day for how long before declaring SRNS?
questions.exp: Steroid (1 mg/kg/day) → 4 months → if no response: SRNS → CNI/MMF → CKD → transplant. (Book p766)

questions.sec: Biopsy & IF: MCD, IgM Nephropathy, FSGS
questions.q: A 12-year-old with steroid-resistant FSGS receives a living-related graft and develops nephrotic-range proteinuria on day 10. The warning printed on this biopsy page that fits is:
opts: Transplant recurrence of FSGS, which can occur even after the kidney is replaced
Hyperacute rejection only, since recurrence is confined to minimal change disease
De-novo membranous nephropathy, the commonest lesion after transplantation
Recurrent IgA nephropathy with mesangial IgA deposits
questions.exp: Even after transplant, recurrence can occur: transplant recurrence FSGS. (Book p766)

questions.sec: Biopsy & IF: MCD, IgM Nephropathy, FSGS
questions.q: Which IF statement is TRUE as per this page?
opts: FSGS IF is linear IgG along the GBM
2° FSGS is IF negative while primary FSGS shows focal IgM ± C3
questions.exp: Focal IgM ± C3 in FSGS; 2° FSGS IF negative; MCD IF normal; IgM +ve belongs to IgM nephropathy. (Book p766)

questions.sec: Biopsy & IF: MCD, IgM Nephropathy, FSGS
questions.q: Match each entity with its IF/biopsy signature — 1) MCD 2) IgM nephropathy 3) Primary FSGS … A) Focal IgM ± C3 B) Normal biopsy and IF C) Mesangial matrix expansion with IgM +ve
questions.exp: MCD normal; IgM nephropathy mesangial expansion + IgM; FSGS focal IgM ± C3. (Book p766)

questions.sec: Biopsy & IF: MCD, IgM Nephropathy, FSGS
questions.q: The light-microscopy figure labels on this page include normal glomerulus (PAS), IgM nephropathy and segmental sclerosis; the odd one out not labelled here is:
questions.exp: Labels: normal glomerulus (PAS), IgM nephropathy, FSGS with segmental sclerosis; spikes belong to the MN pages. (Book p766)

questions.q: The four histological variants of FSGS listed are classical, 2° perihilar, tip variant and:
questions.exp: Variants: classical, 2° perihilar, tip variant, collapsing FSGS. (Book p767)

questions.q: The tip variant FSGS is described with lesion only at tip, features like MCD and:
questions.exp: Tip variant: lesion only at tip; features like MCD; good prognosis. (Book p767)

questions.q: The FSGS variant carrying the worst prognosis is:
questions.exp: Collapsing FSGS: worst prognosis. (Book p767)

questions.q: Each of these is listed as an association of collapsing FSGS EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Associated with: HIV, HIVAN, heroin, IFN α, parvo virus B19, pamidronate. (Book p767)

questions.q: Collapsing FSGS shows complete collapse of glomeruli with hypertrophy of podocyte, nicknamed:
questions.exp: Complete collapse of glomeruli with hypertrophy of podocyte (pseudocrescent); dilated tubules & microcysts. (Book p767)

questions.q: Fill up: The dilated cisternae of endoplasmic reticulum seen on electron microscopy in collapsing FSGS are called ______ footprints.
questions.exp: Electron microscope: dilated cisternae of endoplasmic reticulum (IFN footprints). (Book p767)

questions.q: The note distinguishes the pseudocrescent of collapsing FSGS from the true crescent, which is:
questions.exp: Hypertrophy of parietal epithelial cell: true crescent. (Book p767)

questions.q: Conditions listed with the IFN footprint are SLE and:
questions.exp: Condition with IFN footprint: SLE; FSGS (collapsing variant). (Book p767)

questions.q: All of the following are associated with collapsing FSGS EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Collapsing associations: HIV/HIVAN, heroin, IFN α, parvo B19, pamidronate; gold is an MN drug. (Book p767)

questions.q: Which crescent statement is TRUE as per the note?
opts: Parietal cell hypertrophy forms the pseudocrescent
Hypertrophy of parietal epithelial cell is the true crescent, while podocyte hypertrophy in collapsing FSGS is a pseudocrescent
Podocyte hypertrophy forms the true crescent
questions.exp: Parietal epithelial cell hypertrophy = true crescent; collapsing podocyte hypertrophy = pseudocrescent. (Book p767)

questions.q: The 1959 milestone on the MN antigen timeline is the:
questions.exp: 1959 Heymann nephritis model. (Book p768)

questions.q: The 2009 antigen, usually in primary MN, is:
questions.exp: 2009: M type PLA2R (usually in primary MN). (Book p768)

questions.q: The 2014 antigen, anti-thrombospondin 7A, which can also be seen in secondary MN, is:
questions.exp: 2014: THSD7A, anti thrombospondin 7A (can be seen in secondary MN also). (Book p768)

questions.q: Match each year with its MN antigens — 1) 2019 2) 2020 3) 2021 … A) Neural cell adhesion molecule 1 (NCAM 1), HTRA-1, contactin-1 B) Exostosin 1/2 C) NELL-1, sema 3b, PCDH7
questions.exp: 2019 exostosin 1/2; 2020 NELL-1, sema 3b, PCDH7; 2021 NCAM 1, HTRA-1, contactin-1. (Book p768)

questions.q: The 2020 antigen associated with mercury-containing creams is:
questions.exp: NELL-1: associated with mercury containing creams. (Book p768)

questions.q: The only extrinsic antigen listed in MN is the:
questions.exp: Bovine specific antigen: only extrinsic antigen. (Book p768)

questions.q: The MN rule of 1/3 divides outcomes into spontaneous remission, CKD and:
opts: Continue heavy proteinuria with normal kidney function
questions.exp: 1/3 spontaneous remission; 1/3 continue heavy proteinuria with normal kidney function; 1/3 CKD. (Book p768)

questions.q: On light microscopy, MN shows ↑ thickening of capillary wall, described as:
opts: Uniform thickening of glomerular basement membrane
questions.exp: Uniform thickening of glomerular basement membrane. (Book p768)

questions.q: Match each IF feature with its MN column — 1) 1° MN IgG subclass 2) 2° MN (SLE) IgG subclasses 3) Full house effect … A) + in 2° MN, − in 1° MN B) IgG4 C) IgG1, G2, G3
questions.exp: 1° MN: IgG4; 2° MN (SLE): IgG1, G2, G3 with full house +. (Book p768)

questions.q: In the IF comparison table, anti PLA2R antibody is positive in 1° MN and negative in 2° MN, while mesangial staining is:
questions.exp: Anti PLA2R: − in 2°, + in 1°; mesangial staining: + in 2°, − in 1°. (Book p768)

questions.q: On electron microscopy MN shows effacement of podocytes, subepithelial deposits and spikes; 2° MN additionally deposits in the:
questions.exp: 2° MN: deposits in both subepithelial space & mesangial space. (Book p768)

questions.q: The MN page figures contrast normal thin-walled capillaries with thick capillary walls, show granular IF, and label the schematic with effaced foot processes, thickened basement membrane, subepithelial deposits and:
questions.exp: Schematic labels: podocyte with effaced foot processes, thickened BM, subepithelial deposits, spikes. (Book p769)

questions.q: In the modified Ponticelli regimen for the 70% with NS, steroids are given on months:
questions.exp: Steroids on months 1, 3, 5. (Book p769)

questions.q: Oral cyclophosphamide in the Ponticelli regimen is dosed at 2 mg/kg on months 2, 4, 6, and the regimen ends with:
questions.exp: Oral cyclophosphamide (2 mg/kg) on months 2, 4, 6 → abrupt stop. (Book p769)

questions.q: If there is no response to the Ponticelli regimen, the next agent written is:
questions.exp: Rituximab: if no response to Ponticelli regimen. (Book p769)

questions.q: The 30% asymptomatic MN arm is managed with ACE (−)/ARBs, salt restriction and protein at:
questions.exp: 30% asymptomatic: ACE (−)/ARBs; salt restriction; 1 gm/kg/day protein. (Book p769)

questions.q: Match each MN treatment item with its arm — 1) Modified Ponticelli regimen 2) Rituximab 3) ACE (−)/ARBs … A) 30% asymptomatic arm B) 70% with NS arm C) No response to Ponticelli
questions.exp: 70% with NS → Ponticelli; no response → rituximab; 30% asymptomatic → ACE (−)/ARBs. (Book p769)

questions.q: All of the following belong to the 30% asymptomatic MN arm EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Steroids on months 1, 3, 5 belong to the Ponticelli regimen of the NS arm. (Book p769)

questions.q: Which Ponticelli statement is TRUE as drawn?
opts: Steroids on months 1, 3, 5 alternate with cyclophosphamide on months 2, 4, 6 and the regimen stops abruptly
Steroids and cyclophosphamide run together every month
questions.exp: Steroids months 1, 3, 5; cyclophosphamide months 2, 4, 6; abrupt stop. (Book p769)

questions.sec: MN figures, IF & the treatment split · p769
questions.q: In the Ponticelli arm of the treatment chart, oral cyclophosphamide is given at 2 mg/kg on which months?
questions.exp: Steroids are printed as 'On months 1,3,5' and oral cyclophosphamide (2 mg/kg) as 'On months 2,4,6', with the two brackets closing on 'Abrupt stop'. (Book p769)

questions.sec: MN figures, IF & the treatment split · p769
questions.q: Fill up: The bracket that groups the alternating steroid and cyclophosphamide months in the modified Ponticelli regimen ends with the instruction ______ stop.
questions.exp: The brace beside the two drug lines is captioned 'Abrupt stop', i.e. the alternating cycles are stopped rather than tapered on this page. (Book p769)

questions.sec: MN figures, IF & the treatment split · p769
questions.q: Match each label of the membranous nephropathy diagram with what it points to — 1) Podocyte 2) Basement membrane 3) Deposits … A) Effaced foot processes B) Thickened C) Subepithelial, with spikes
questions.exp: The diagram is labelled Podocyte with effaced foot processes, Thickened basement membrane, Subepithelial deposits and Spikes, and is captioned 'membranous nephropathy'. (Book p769)

questions.sec: MN figures, IF & the treatment split · p769
questions.q: The green capillary-loop photograph on this page carries which caption?
questions.exp: The immunofluorescence photograph along the glomerular capillary loops is captioned 'IF in MN', sitting between the two light-microscopy photographs and the labelled diagram. (Book p769)

questions.sec: MN figures, IF & the treatment split · p769
questions.q: A 45-year-old with biopsy-proven MN has only trace proteinuria, normal albumin and no edema. Per the treatment chart's right-hand arm, the plan is:
opts: Modified Ponticelli regimen with steroids on months 1, 3 and 5
Rituximab, since MN always needs B-cell depletion
Renal biopsy repeat before any drug is started
ACE inhibitor or ARB, salt restriction and 1 gm/kg/day protein
questions.exp: The 30% asymptomatic arm is managed with ACE(−)/ARBs, salt restriction and 1 gm/kg/day protein; the Ponticelli regimen and rituximab belong to the 70% who present with nephrotic syndrome. (Book p769)

units.title: Podocytopathy types & MCD causes/presentation
units.guide: Definition and presentation list, the without/with-podocytopenia split (MCD no CKD risk; FSGS >2/3; MN 1/3; DN), MCD 2° causes (NSAIDs MCD>MN vs gold MN>MCD, interferon α; atopy/post-immunization; Hodgkin's/Sezary/CLL) and the 100/0 rule with absent HTN/AKI/microhematuria.

units.title: FSGS causes, circulating factors & genetic forms
units.guide: 2° FSGS drug/infection/misc lists, suPAR + CLC-1 as circulating permeability factor, congenital NS genetics (NPHS1-nephrin birth/DMS; NPHS2-podocin 3-5 yrs; α actin 4/TRPC 6 AD adolescents) with transplant-only Rx, and 2° perihilar hyperfiltration mechanics with ACE (−).

units.title: 75/25 rule & MN causes
units.guide: FSGS 75/25 rule with the no-immunosuppression instruction, the full MN 2° cause tree (drugs incl. mercury; HBV/syphilis/schistosomiasis; SLE V, RA amyloid>MN, sarcoid/IgG4 tubulointerstitial, rare trio; colorectal adenocarcinoma), anti-PLA2R, 70/30 rule with maximum thrombosis, d-penicillamine note and adult-MN/child-MCD mnemonics.

units.title: MCD features, podocyte changes & treatment flowchart
units.sec: MCD Features, Podocyte Changes & Relapse · p765
units.guide: Lipoid nephrosis with 90%/10-15% shares, boys>girls peak 2-7 yrs, non-selective proteinuria vs selective albumin/transferrin, CD80/angiopoietin-like 4 charge loss, URTI/LRTI relapse with 0.5 mg/kg prednisolone, the 4-week steroid flowchart (5-10% resistance → biopsy/genetics → CNI or transplant; 25/25/50 responder split), FRNS cyclophosphamide and SDNS MMF-best/rituximab.

units.title: Biopsy & IF: MCD, IgM nephropathy, FSGS
units.sec: Biopsy & IF: MCD, IgM Nephropathy, FSGS · p766
units.guide: Normal LM/IF in MCD; IgM nephropathy variant (mesangial expansion, IgM +ve, poorer prognosis); FSGS Apo L1 and 70% CKD by 10 yrs; focal/segmental definitions; podocytopenia-synechiae sclerosis chain; focal IgM ± C3 with 2° IF negative; 1 mg/kg/day × 4 months ladder to transplant and transplant-recurrence FSGS.

units.title: FSGS histological variants
units.guide: Classical, 2° perihilar, tip variant (tip-only, MCD-like, good) and collapsing (worst; HIV/HIVAN, heroin, IFN α, parvo B19, pamidronate; pseudocrescent podocyte hypertrophy, dilated tubules/microcysts, ER cisternae = IFN footprints) plus the true-crescent note and SLE/collapsing IFN-footprint pair.

units.title: MN antigens, rule of thirds & biopsy/IF/EM
units.sec: MN Antigens & Rule of Thirds · p768
units.guide: The antigen road-map (1959 Heymann → 2009 PLA2R → 2014 THSD7A → 2019 exostosin → 2020 NELL-1/sema 3b/PCDH7 → 2021 NCAM1/HTRA-1/contactin-1), bovine extrinsic antigen, 1/3 outcomes, uniform GBM thickening, the 1° vs 2° IF table (IgG4 vs IgG1-3, full house, PLA2R, mesangial staining) and subepithelial deposits/spikes with 2° mesangial extension.

units.title: MN figures, IF and the two treatment arms
units.guide: Figure contrast (normal thin capillary walls vs thickened walls in membranous glomerulopathy), the IF-in-MN photograph and the labelled schematic (podocyte with effaced foot processes, thickened basement membrane, subepithelial deposits, spikes); treatment splits 70% with NS on modified Ponticelli (steroids months 1,3,5; oral cyclophosphamide 2 mg/kg months 2,4,6; abrupt stop; rituximab on failure) vs 30% asymptomatic (ACE inhibitors/ARBs, salt restriction, 1 gm/kg/day protein).
